subject: Multigroup SEM: "covariance matrix is not positive" error

messages.author: 913d6223762c1a08
messages.subject: Multigroup SEM: "covariance matrix is not positive" error
parts:
Hello,

I'm a bit of a novice at lavaan and SEM and was hoping for some assistance. I am an ecologist and I am investigating the effects that four species traits have on the variability of species' position in the network through time. Thus, because we have repeated entry of each species in which the variability (y) is different, I am using the group argument inside the sem function. However, the other traits are constant, since they are measured at the species level. 

I am testing two different relationships between the variables: one in which abundance and phenology also affect rdegree, and the other one in which all traits directly affect the response variable y (variability).

But, it is not working. I get the error: 

Error in lav_samplestats_icov(COV = cov[[g]], ridge = ridge, x.idx = x.idx[[g]],  : 
  lavaan ERROR: sample covariance matrix is not positive-definite

Attached is my code and some data to run it. 

Any tips would be greatly appreciated!

Best,
Marilia
--
Marilia P. Gaiarsa 
Postdoctoral researcher, Ponisio Lab
University of California Riverside

messages.subject: Re: Multigroup SEM: "covariance matrix is not positive" error

Thus, because we have repeated entry of each
species in which the variability (y) is different, I am using the

constant, since they are measured at the species level.

You have 21 groups!  All of them, arguably, have sample sizes too low for SEM (which is based on asymptotic theory).

table(data.spp$spp)
 a  b  d  e  f  i  j  k  l  m  n  o  p  q  r  s  t  u  v  w  y 
 9  8  9  6 10  8 27 18 38 41 14 18  6 41 15 14  6  8 22  5 29 

Given the number of groups, this seems like a multilevel situation. As you describe, only your outcome is a Level-1 variable, so a multigroup model will not work because all your predictors/mediators have 0 variability within group/cluster:

aggregate(cbind(abund, phen, rdeg, dprim, y) ~ spp, data = data.spp, sd)

With multilevel SEM, your Level-1 sample size is 352, but your Level-2 sample size is quite low (21).  It might run, but I doubt you could trust your results with so little information.  

http://users.ugent.be/~yrosseel/lavaan/zurich2017/INTRO/lavaan_intro_zurich2017.pdf 

Preacher et al. (2010) would be a good read for you.  The talk about MSEM for mediation, and their Example 2 application is a 2-2-1 design (like yours).

Preacher, K. J., Zyphur, M. J., & Zhang, Z. (2010). A general multilevel SEM framework for assessing multilevel mediation. Psychological Methods, 15(3), 209-233. doi:10.1037/a0020141

They posted Mplus syntax in an online appendix:

http://quantpsy.org/pubs/syntax_appendix_081311.pdf

But you should be able to fit that model in lavaan (again, if it converges on so little data).
